never: type a due date by hand, or use a date somebody typed onto the job
guess an install date, a model, an equipment type, a schedule or a warranty term the record does not hold
remind a customer who already has a job open for that asset
message a customer on a channel they did not agree to, or anyone who asked to stop
send more than one reminder and one follow-up for a date
say what a warranty covers, that a repair is covered, or anything about the customer's rights
write a second booking request for the same asset and date
pick a time slot or a price
stays_with_person: booking the time and pricing the work for every booking request
writing and changing the service schedule
fixing a record with a missing install date, model or type
answering any reply that is not a yes or a stop
anything about warranty cover or consumer rights

provider_block.job: every unit you installed or serviced gets a reminder before it is due, and a yes becomes one booking request

with_us.note: No hosted step. Writing each yes into the live job system as exactly one booking request against the right customer and asset, safe to retry, is the step not to hand-roll, and it is quoted as a scoped build on the job system the business already runs. Tradify has no public API, so it cannot meet that check live.

checks.title: The equipment is taken from the finished job, as recorded
A missing install date, model or equipment type goes to a person
Due dates are worked out from the schedule, never typed in
The warranty expiry comes from the term on the record
One reminder, a written lead time ahead of each date
Only on a channel the customer agreed to
One follow-up if there is no answer, then stop
A stop is honoured for good, on every asset
A warranty reminder states the expiry date and nothing about cover
A yes becomes one booking request in the job system
The build never picks a time or a price
Every reminder, reply and booking is on the record, by asset
